title: Acute limb ischaemia — threatened limb
logic: Limb with pain, pallor, pulselessness, coldness AND either sensory loss or muscle weakness/tenderness (Rutherford IIa/IIb pattern)
action: Emergency pathway: anticoagulate on diagnosis per protocol, keep the limb dependent-neutral and warm, nil by mouth, theatre/transfer for revascularisation within the 6-hour warm-ischaemia window; record onset time prominently; fixed mottling with rigid muscles reroutes to amputation counselling, not revascularisation

title: Post-revascularisation compartment syndrome and reperfusion injury
logic: Revascularisation after more than 4 hours of ischaemia AND (increasing calf pain/tension OR dark urine OR rising potassium)
action: Urgent senior review for fasciotomy if not already done; send potassium and creatine kinase, monitor urine output and colour; alert for arrhythmia from hyperkalaemia; do not attribute new calf pain post-embolectomy to the wound

title: Loss of arteriovenous fistula thrill
logic: Patient with an AV fistula reports absent thrill/buzz, or staff find no thrill or bruit on examination
action: Same-day referral to the access surgeon/dialysis unit — early thrombosis is salvageable within hours; do not schedule to routine clinic; document last-known-patent time

title: Diabetic foot severity grading required
logic: Diabetic foot ulcer or infection recorded AND no severity grade (Wagner or equivalent local scale) captured
action: Prompt grading at first assessment and at each operative event; grade 3 and above (deep abscess/osteomyelitis/gangrene) routes to same-day surgical review rather than dressing clinic

title: Arterial assessment before compression or ulcer surgery
logic: Compression bandaging prescribed or venous ulcer surgery booked AND no arterial assessment recorded (palpable pedal pulses or ankle-brachial index)
action: Block the compression/surgery order until pedal pulses or ABI documented; ABI below 0.8 (or absent pulses) reroutes to arterial work-up — compression over an ischaemic limb causes necrosis

title: Ischaemia time captured for vascular trauma
logic: Vascular injury with ischaemia recorded AND injury time or reperfusion time missing from the operative record
action: Require both timestamps before record completion; auto-compute ischaemia duration and surface it on the post-operative monitoring plan (drives fasciotomy vigilance)

title: Heparinisation before arterial clamping
logic: Elective/urgent arterial reconstruction or embolectomy operative record completed AND no intra-operative heparin (or documented contraindication) recorded before clamp application
action: Prompt the team to record systemic heparin administration prior to clamping, or the explicit bleeding-risk contraindication that replaced it (with regional/local flush alternative noted)

title: Vein-preservation flag for CKD patients
logic: Patient with CKD stage 4-5 or planned dialysis AND any order for IV cannulation/phlebotomy on the planned access arm (non-dominant forearm/cephalic system)
action: Surface a vein-preservation banner on the patient record: no cannulas, blood draws or blood-pressure cuffs on the flagged arm; suggest dorsum-of-hand or dominant arm alternatives

title: Post-revascularisation perfusion observations
logic: Arterial repair, bypass or embolectomy completed within the past 48 hours
action: Schedule perfusion checks (colour, warmth, capillary refill, pedal Doppler signal, pain) hourly for 6 hours then 4-hourly; any lost signal or new pain triggers immediate surgeon notification — early graft/artery thrombosis is salvageable

title: Amputation aftercare bundle
logic: Major limb amputation performed AND discharge planned without prosthetic/rehabilitation referral, stump-care instruction, and contralateral-foot review recorded
action: Block discharge checklist completion until physiotherapy/prosthetics referral, stump bandaging education, phantom-pain counselling and an examination of the remaining foot (for diabetics) are documented; book wound review and suture removal at 2-3 weeks
